failure_summary: V3 did not author pixel art. It mechanically isolated the high-resolution three-quarter reference, downscaled it to 128 px visible height, reused the reduced reference silhouette/mask, quantized colors and applied local cleanup. The result therefore reads as a tiny reduced illustration/render rather than intentional modern pixel art.
method_failures: high-resolution reference silhouette mechanically survives into the candidate instead of being independently authored as native 2D character art
LANCZOS reduction followed by palette quantization is exactly the class of reduced-illustration/pixel-filter approach already forbidden as a production-art method
palette reduction and majority cleanup do not create intentional pixel clusters or authored anatomy
the spike therefore cannot meaningfully validate the required authored pixel-art language
visual_failures: reads as a miniaturized render rather than character pixel art
hands, feet and face collapse at native scale
anatomical masses are inherited from reduction rather than deliberately redesigned for the pixel grid
value structure remains render-like and noisy rather than grouped into intentional clusters
no useful production pixel-language decision is proven
model_cleanup_reason: V3 downloaded no model weights and used only existing Python/Pillow tooling.
next_rule: The next B3B candidate must begin as actual authored native pixel character art. The approved high-resolution nude turnaround may guide anatomy/proportion/identity but must not be resized, traced mechanically, quantized or used as direct final silhouette authority.
